headline: Wall Street opens risk-off as the chip sell-off crosses the Atlantic
tone: The US open has turned this morning's regional chip shakeout into a pre-Nvidia de-risking, and a soft factory survey gave buyers no reason to step in.
body: The test from midday failed: the Nasdaq followed Asia's chip names lower at the open. Micron, Intel and AMD are falling harder than Nvidia itself, so this is the whole AI-hardware trade being cut before Tuesday night's results, not just a vote on Nvidia's leadership row (the FT report on a Jensen Huang comeback and Treasury Secretary Bessent's call for an outside CEO).

The 14:30 data did not help. The New York Fed's Empire State index fell 18 points to 7.8, against 16.7 expected; it still signals growth, but it removes the soft-landing cushion that could have offset the tech selling. The Dow's value names holding up shows rotation rather than a broad dash for cash.

Europe is still acting as the anti-AI trade, with healthcare and the Swiss defensives in demand, while basic resources lag on weak Chinese activity data. Copper miners and silver are being sold alongside tech, a sign the selling is about growth and crowded positions, not one sector.

Oil has slipped further since midday: Reuters says recovering Hormuz flows and the IEA's fourth-quarter surplus call are now outweighing Iran's strike on Bahrain and new tanker mine hits. Chinese refinery runs dropping 8.1% year on year in October add to the demand worry.

views.text: Tone is risk-off into Nvidia's results (Tuesday, about 22:20 Zurich). What would change it: Fed Chair Warsh's speech at 18:00 Zurich sounding relaxed about growth, or a clear answer on Nvidia's CEO search before the print.

The market now trades the surplus, not the war. Only a hit to Gulf loading terminals or a halt in Hormuz traffic would bring the risk premium back; diesel stays the tightest part of the barrel into winter.
